crm_notes:
- Account: Avalon (large fintech platform). Primary contact: CTO-level procurement + infra ops. Short notes / bullets from calls.
- Use-case: real-time risk scoring + trader-assist chat. Latency critical during market hours (08:00-18:00 ET). 75% of calls are short chat completions + embeddings for contextual signals.
- Customer ask (verbatim): "we cannot accept > 5min of aggregated downtime during market hours per month" — interpreted as high uptime needs.
- Key tech asks: P95 < 200ms for chat inference on standard prompt (<= 512 tokens), P99 < 500ms for tail; throughput target ~ 800 requests/min steady, spikes to 3k/min during open.
- Planned reservation: want 16 reserved GPUs (A100-equivalent) with autoscale to 24 for bursts. Request burst credit accounting and predictable cost for bursting.
- SLA negotiation points: uptime target, credit schedule for breaches, maintenance windows (no maintenance during US market hours; prefer Sat 02:00-06:00 UTC), emergency maintenance policy, advance notice windows (48–72h), and blackout days (end-of-quarter reporting days).
- Support: require 24/7 P1 on-call with 15-minute response and SRE escalation path; P2 1 hour; P3 4 hours. Also want monthly runbooks and quarterly DR drills.
- Security/compliance: require SOC2 + ISO27001 evidence, SSO/SAML integration, audit logs retention (7 years for certain datasets), KMS key wrap and BYOK option for private deployments.
- Legal: pushing for SLA credit schedule over monetary refunds; Avalon prefers credits applied to monthly invoice. They asked for a 12-month trial period for SLA metrics.
- POC milestone: 2-week pilot (Dec) to validate latency under synthetic load, then 60-day pilot on live anonymized traffic.
- Quote: preliminary reserved pricing shared; they asked for a +10% discount if commit to 12-month reserved capacity.
- Next internal: align with Pricing and Legal on credit % bands and emergency maintenance language.
sla_negotiation_summary: Avalon requires a firm SLA for Dedicated capacity. Current ask: 99.95% monthly uptime for mission-critical endpoints during market hours. Redwood proposal (draft): tiered credit schedule — uptime >= 99.95% = no credit; 99.9%–99.95% = 10% monthly service credit; 99.0%–99.9% = 25% credit; <99.0% = 50% credit and option to terminate after 30 days if recurring. Avalon counters: wants narrower bands and credits applied as service credits with right to escalate. Legal redlines focus on liability cap and termination notice. Need to finalize: measurement window (UTC month vs rolling 30d), exclusion events, and credit payout mechanics.
reserved_gpu_plan: Initial conservative plan: 16 A100-equivalent reserved (steady state) with autoscale headroom to 24 for burst. Suggested split: 12 inference-heavy nodes (low-latency), 4 KV/cache accelerators, 4 warm standby for failover. Need to agree on burst CPU/GPU credit accounting and billing for burst minutes. Also discussed quantization options to reduce GPU footprint by ~30% if model accuracy budget allows.
latency_throughput_slos: Target SLOs discussed with customer: P95 <= 200ms, P99 <= 500ms for standard chat prompts (<=512 tokens). Throughput target: sustained 800 req/min with ability to handle 3k/min spikes. Agreed to define test harness (synthetic + replay of anonymized production trace) for validation. Redwood to provide baseline telemetry and token-level cost breakdown to inform sizing.
maintenance_policy_proposal: Proposed maintenance policy: regular maintenance windows up to 2 hours/month, scheduled with 72-hour notice, default weekend UTC window Sat 02:00-06:00. No scheduled maintenance allowed during customer-declared blackout windows (market open hours and end-of-quarter). Emergency maintenance permitted with 48-hour notice when possible; immediate emergency takes place only for security-critical fixes and will be communicated via phone + email. Avalon requests formal amendment forbidding scheduled maintenance during 08:00-18:00 ET on trading days.
support_response_times: Requested SLAs: P1 (sev: platform down impacting trading) — initial response <= 15 minutes, next update every 30 minutes, target resolution or workaround within 4 hours; P2 (degraded performance) — initial response <= 1 hour, target resolution 24 hours; P3 (minor/feature) — initial response <= 4 hours, resolution per roadmap. Redwood proposed 24/7 on-call for P1 and dedicated SE during market hours. Action: produce formal support matrix for contract.
legal_risk_and_price_notes: Legal: termination clause (Avalon wants 30 days with cause for repeated SLA misses), Redwood standard is 60 days; liability cap negotiation ongoing. Price: Redwood proposed reserved discount tiers (10% for 12mo, 18% for 24mo) + monthly burst buffer priced per GPU-minute. Avalon pushing for credit-first remediation vs cash refunds. Finance to confirm impact of credits on ARR recognition.
